properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): reflow2's only served "export before you finish" line comes from a seat's tracked-export records, and a hosted store never has one. So on flo2 loop_status says nothing about exports, exactly as on a local store nobody has exported, and get_instructions is the local text byte for byte. The accepted 2026-09-27 rules say no export is owed on a served design; no served text says so
properties.statement:
① OBSERVED (dev_storyflow session 62995724, 2026-09-27, the day StoryFlow's design moved onto flo2.io). The reporter wrote: the project's rule `rule:the_export_is_the_only_durable_copy_export_before_you_finish` "assumes a local store; the hosted server should say (in `loop_status` or `get_instructions`) whether an export is still owed". Expected: a hosted session can tell whether it owes an export. NOT affected: sync_status on api.flo2.io, which flo2 answers itself ("No copy of <design> is tracked here … an export is a copy at one moment that nothing tracks").

② SEARCHED the raw words in both designs. reflow2 already holds the answer in substance. dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy (accepted 2026-09-27) says, in its rule 3, that an export is a copy reflow2 never tracks, and in its rule 6 that backup is of stores and is the operator's job (dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer). epoch:planned-flo2-then-reflow2-move-and-the-photocopy-retires (planned) retires the tracked-export machinery, and req:a-photocopy-says-it-is-one (accepted) makes every export say it is a copy. flo2 holds cap:nightly-consistent-backup-pulled-off-the-box plus off-site copies. No record says any served text tells a session any of this.

③ CANDIDATES.
(a) STALENESS: the served text predates the 09-27 rules.
(b) CONTRACT: loop_status's only export sentence comes from the seat's tracked-export records. It has no branch for "no record here, and none is owed", so its silence cannot be read.
(c) ALLOCATION: the durability fact (the nightly store backup) belongs to the host. reflow2 cannot know it, and flo2's door does not state it where a session reads (recorded in flo2's design as the second instance of fact:root-cause-the-door-rebinds-approver-and-says-so-only-in-its-refusal-2026-09-28).
(d) NOT IN REFLOW2: the rule is StoryFlow's own and outlived the local store it was written for.
(e) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: loop_status on a hosted store does speak about exports.

④ WHAT WOULD TELL THEM APART. (e) predicts a registry-served loop_status mentions exports. (b) predicts silence on hosted and on a never-exported local store alike, with the sentence appearing only once an export is tracked. (a) alone predicts get_instructions differs between hosted and local, or says something about exports.

⑤ RESULT (0.72.0, scratch stores, 2026-09-28).
- Registry engine (`--registry-root … --http`, /g/<id>/mcp): loop_status has no `sync` key and no export line in `next`. Its artifacts block does say "this server does not hold the project tree (an in-memory or registry-served design …)".
- Local store with the same content, never exported: the same silence.
- The same local store after export_graph to a path and one more write: `next` gains "This graph holds 4 node(s) … 1 node(s) here are in no record. A record is the only copy that survives losing the graph directory: export before you finish."
- get_instructions is byte-identical local versus hosted (28,838 chars). That includes "The graph lives at `.reflow2/graph`" and restoring with `--graph-path … --import`. There is no hosted or durability wording.
Verdicts. (e) REFUTED. (b) CONFIRMED. (a) CONFIRMED, but it would not suffice on its own: even current text would be silent here, because the one line is gated on tracked records. The StoryFlow rule's wording ("the export is the only durable copy … export before you finish") matches reflow2's served sentence, so the project rule is most likely that sentence adopted as a rule. That bears on (d).

⑥ CLASS. This is an instance of fact:root-cause-the-served-text-describes-one-deployment-and-a-host-changes-the-rules-under-it-2026-09-28. The one sentence about durability depends on local machinery, so on a hosted engine silence stands for "nothing tracked", and the agent cannot tell that from "nothing owed" or "not checked". reflow2 already knows the design is registry-served (the NoTree note above), and it uses that for files but not for exports. Would changing the sentence alone have stopped this? No: the sentence is never reached on a hosted store.

⑦ Out of scope. A class-pinning test would assert: on a design served without its tree, loop_status always carries an explicit answer about exports and durability (never absent, and different from a local store's). It would also assert that the handshake and get_instructions served for such a design contain no `.reflow2/graph` or `--graph-path` step unless it is marked local-only. The test should check that an answer is present, not its wording.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. What the StoryFlow store on flo2 actually answers: not called, because flo2.io calls are logged against the person. It follows from the code and from the scratch measurement. Whether StoryFlow's rule was copied from reflow2's sentence: only the wording matches. What loss window flo2's nightly backup means for a session is flo2's to state.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. "Nothing tells the session whether an export is still owed" HELD. "The hosted server should say it in loop_status or get_instructions": both are reflow2's, and both are silent or local-only on a hosted store. Whether the answer belongs there, in flo2's preamble, or in both is open in dec:idea-loop-status-says-whether-an-export-is-owed-on-a-hosted-design.
